description: Governed engineering and evaluation tags for the XLAI Safety Corpus. Tags describe test purpose and are independent of exposure role.

tags.description: Tests interpretation of the current message or turn.
Tests transfer beyond an exposed wording or scenario instance.
Tests meaning changes caused by surrounding context.
Represents safety-adjacent language that should remain below a safety threshold.
Guards against escalating non-safety language into safety handling.
Guards against missing supported safety evidence.
Uses humor, joking, sarcasm, or exaggerated language as context.
Contains a retraction after a concerning or ambiguous statement.
Contains language that minimizes or masks a possible safety concern.
Tests meanings of disappearance, leaving, or not returning.
Concerns location sharing, checking, or requests for location access.
Concerns punishment, restricted autonomy, or control backed by consequences.
Concerns unwanted location, device, movement, or communication monitoring.
Concerns self-harm or suicide-related language.
Concerns possible physical harm toward another person.
Concerns current or imminent life-threatening danger.
Contains language attributed to another speaker or source.
Contains fictional story, movie, game, or character language.
Reports language or behavior from a third party.
Uses conversation history rather than one isolated message.
Tests how later evidence changes or confirms an earlier interpretation.
Tests a change toward greater conflict, safety concern, or immediacy.
Uses an observable or explicitly limited communication baseline.
Represents a recurring interaction sequence without diagnosing participants.
Preserves materially plausible interpretations or incomplete evidence.
Useful for comparing semantic annotation with deterministic runtime output.
